cards.title: Reading Comprehension, Context Clues
rule: Reading Comprehension, Context Clues & Reference Words

Definition: Reading Comprehension & Reference tracking (ናይ ምንባብን ምግንዛብን ክእለት) refers to the cognitive strategies of skimming for main ideas, scanning for specific details, using surrounding semantic context clues to decode unfamiliar vocabulary, and tracing reference words (pronouns and determiners) to their correct nouns or clausal antecedents.

Reading comprehension is a critical component of the national matriculation examination, accounting for a significant portion of the total English score. Successful reading requires mastering skimming (ብላዕሊ ላዕሊ ምንባብ) and scanning (ሰሊኽካ ፍሉይ ሓበሬታ ምድላይ). Skimming ($$\text{Skimming} \rightarrow \text{Main Idea / Title}$$) is the rapid reading of introductory and concluding paragraphs, along with topic sentences, to grasp the general theme of a passage. Scanning ($$\text{Scanning} \rightarrow \text{Specific details / Names / Dates}$$) involves moving one's eyes rapidly over the text to locate specific keywords, dates, or figures without reading every word. Tigrinya speakers often struggle with reading speed because they perform subvocalization (ብውሽጢ ምድማጽ) or mental translation (ብኣእምሮ ምትርጓም), which slows down their processing. Students must train themselves to bypass word-by-word translation to improve their reading efficiency.

body: Reading Comprehension, Context Clues & Reference Words

Definition: Reading Comprehension & Reference tracking (ናይ ምንባብን ምግንዛብን ክእለት) refers to the cognitive strategies of skimming for main ideas, scanning for specific details, using surrounding semantic context clues to decode unfamiliar vocabulary, and tracing reference words (pronouns and determiners) to their correct nouns or clausal antecedents.

Reading comprehension is a critical component of the national matriculation examination, accounting for a significant portion of the total English score. Successful reading requires mastering skimming (ብላዕሊ ላዕሊ ምንባብ) and scanning (ሰሊኽካ ፍሉይ ሓበሬታ ምድላይ). Skimming ($$\text{Skimming} \rightarrow \text{Main Idea / Title}$$) is the rapid reading of introductory and concluding paragraphs, along with topic sentences, to grasp the general theme of a passage. Scanning ($$\text{Scanning} \rightarrow \text{Specific details / Names / Dates}$$) involves moving one's eyes rapidly over the text to locate specific keywords, dates, or figures without reading every word. Tigrinya speakers often struggle with reading speed because they perform subvocalization (ብውሽጢ ምድማጽ) or mental translation (ብኣእምሮ ምትርጓም), which slows down their processing. Students must train themselves to bypass word-by-word translation to improve their reading efficiency.

Deducing the meaning of unfamiliar words using context clues (ኩነታዊ ትርጉም ምፍላይ) is a highly valued exam skill. Examiners frequently underline difficult academic words in passages and ask for their closest meaning. Students can use four types of context clues: - Synonym clues: the text provides a similar word nearby. - Antonym/Contrast clues: the text uses contrast markers like *however, although, whereas* ($$\text{Unfamiliar Word} + \text{Contrast Marker} \rightarrow \text{Antonym Clue}$$).

cards.title: Worked practice
cards.problem:
Read the context and answer the question:
'The ministry launched a new educational portal last week. **It** was designed to provide free learning modules for high school students.'
The pronoun 'It' refers to:

steps.text: 'It' is a singular neuter subject pronoun.
Its antecedent must be a singular inanimate noun phrase mentioned in the preceding sentence.

cards.title: Quick check
cards.q:
Read the context and answer the question:
'The ministry launched a new educational portal last week. **It** was designed to provide free learning modules for high school students.'
The pronoun 'It' refers to:
cards.why:
**Step 1: Analyze the grammatical structure**
'It' is a singular neuter subject pronoun. Its antecedent must be a singular inanimate noun phrase mentioned in the preceding sentence.

**Step 2: Identify the matriculation trap**
Students might choose 'the ministry' (singular) or 'free learning modules' (plural). By applying the Pronoun Substitution Test ('The new educational portal was designed to...'), Option B is clearly correct.

**Step 3: Tigrinya Explanation (ትርጉም)**
'It' (ንሱ - ዘይህይወታዊ ነጸላ) ዝብል ተውላጠ ስም ንሓደ ቅድሚኡ ዝተገልጸ ነጸላ ስም እዩ ዝውክል። ነቲ ሓረግ 'The new educational portal was designed...' (እቲ ሓድሽ መርበብ ሓበሬታ...) ኢልና ክንተክኦ ከለና ግቡእ ትርጉም ስለ ዝህብ፡ ቅኑዕ መልሲ Option B እዩ።

cards.title: Worked practice
cards.problem:
Choose the closest contextual meaning of the underlined word:
'The professor's lecture was exceptionally **succinct**; he covered the entire complex topic in only five minutes.'

steps.text: The context clue 'in only five minutes' indicates that the lecture was very short and concise.

cards.title: Quick check
cards.q:
Choose the closest contextual meaning of the underlined word:
'The professor's lecture was exceptionally **succinct**; he covered the entire complex topic in only five minutes.'
cards.why:
**Step 1: Analyze the grammatical structure**
The context clue 'in only five minutes' indicates that the lecture was very short and concise. We need a synonym for 'succinct'.

**Step 2: Identify the matriculation trap**
Students often guess 'detailed' (Option A) because of 'complex topic'. However, the time clue ('five minutes') confirms that 'brief' (Option B) is the correct meaning.

**Step 3: Tigrinya Explanation (ትርጉም)**
'Succinct' (ሓጺርን ንጹርን) ዝብል ቃል፡ ንሓደ ተግባር ብሓጺርን ብቑርጥን መገዲ ክግለጽ ከሎ የውክል ኩነታዊ መርትዖና ድማ 'in only five minutes' (ንሓሙሽተ ደቓይቕ ጥራይ) ዝብል ስለ ዝኾነ፡ ቅኑዕ ትርጉሙ 'brief' (Option B - ሓጺር) እዩ።

cards.title: Worked practice
cards.problem:
Read the context and answer the question:
'The candidates completed their laboratory tests. The program coordinator congratulated them on **their** outstanding results.'
The possessive pronoun 'their' refers to:

steps.text: It must refer back to a plural noun denoting owners, which is 'candidates' (the people who achieved the results).

cards.title: Quick check
cards.q:
Read the context and answer the question:
'The candidates completed their laboratory tests. The program coordinator congratulated them on **their** outstanding results.'
The possessive pronoun 'their' refers to:
cards.why:
**Step 1: Analyze the grammatical structure**
'Their' is a plural possessive pronoun. It must refer back to a plural noun denoting owners, which is 'candidates' (the people who achieved the results).

**Step 2: Identify the matriculation trap**
Students might confuse 'their' with the plural 'laboratory tests' or 'results'. The context shows that the results belonged to the candidates, making Option B correct.

**Step 3: Tigrinya Explanation (ትርጉም)**
'Their' (ናታቶም - ናይ ብዙሕ ወንነት) ዝብል ተውላጠ ስም ን ብዙሓት ሰባት እዩ ዝውክል። እቲ ውጽኢት ናይቶም 'candidates' (ሕጹያት/ተመሃሮ) ስለ ዝኾነ፡ እቲ ተውላጠ ስም ንዓኣቶም ይውክል፤ ስለዚ ቅኑዕ መልሲ Option B እዩ።

questions.q:
Choose the closest contextual meaning of the underlined word:
'The chemistry laboratory was filled with **noxious** fumes—gases that are highly poisonous to inhale.'
questions.label: 6. Choose the closest contextual meaning of the underlined word
why: Answer B: poisonous
**Step 1: Analyze the grammatical structure**
The sentence directly defines 'noxious' after the em-dash (—) as 'gases that are highly poisonous to inhale'. This is a definition context clue.

'The regional government increased the high school budget last month. **This** allowed the principal to build new labs.'
The pronoun 'This' refers to:
questions.label:
7. Read the context and answer the question:
'The regional gove

**Step 1: Analyze the grammatical structure**
The demonstrative pronoun 'This' refers back to the entire clause action mentioned in the preceding sentence: 'The regional government increased the high school budget'.
**Step 2: Identify the matriculation trap**
questions.tip: Eliminate options that break the grammar rule first.

questions.q:
Choose the closest contextual meaning of the underlined word:
'The forest is home to various **indigenous** plants, such as native acacia and local papyrus.'
questions.label: 8. Choose the closest contextual meaning of the underlined word
why: Answer B: native
**Step 1: Analyze the grammatical structure**
The sentence provides example clues introduced by 'such as', using synonyms like 'native acacia' and 'local papyrus' to clarify the meaning of 'indigenous'.
**Step 2: Identify the matriculation trap**
questions.tip: Eliminate options that break the grammar rule first.

The pronoun 'them' refers to:
questions.label:

'The library purch
why: Answer B: reference books
**Step 1: Analyze the grammatical structure**
'Them' is a plural object pronoun. Its antecedent must be a plural noun phrase in the preceding sentence, which is 'reference books'.
**Step 2: Identify the matriculation trap**

questions.q:
Choose the closest contextual meaning of the underlined word:
'Aster was **resolute** in her decision to study chemistry; however, her brother was completely wavering.'
questions.label: 10. Choose the closest contextual meaning of the underlined word
why: Answer A: firm
**Step 1: Analyze the grammatical structure**
The contrastive conjunction 'however' indicates that 'resolute' is the opposite of 'wavering' (undecided/weak).
**Step 2: Identify the matriculation trap**

questions.q: "The medicine was so potent that a single drop was enough to cure the fever." What does "potent" mean?
questions.label: 11. "The medicine was so potent that a single drop was enough to cure the fever." What does "potent"…

similar.q: Meaning of "feeble" in "His feeble voice could hardly be heard".

why: Answer B: powerful
"a single drop was enough to cure the fever" shows great strength.
So "potent" means powerful.
"weak" is the opposite; "sweet" and "cheap" are unrelated.
questions.tip: Use context clues: definitions, synonyms, contrast words (but, unlike, however) and examples (such as). Answer from the passage, not from your own opinion.

questions.q: "Unlike his frugal brother, who saves every Nakfa, Yonas spends money freely." What does "frugal" mean?
questions.label: 12. "Unlike his frugal brother, who saves every Nakfa, Yonas spends money freely." What does "frugal"…

similar.q: Context clue type in this sentence.
similar.a: contrast (Unlike) and definition (who saves every Nakfa).

why: Answer D: careful with money
"Unlike" signals contrast with "spends money freely".
"who saves every Nakfa" defines frugal directly.
So frugal means careful with money.
questions.tip: Use context clues: definitions, synonyms, contrast words (but, unlike, however) and examples (such as). Answer from the passage, not from your own opinion.

questions.q: Read: "Desertification, the process by which fertile land becomes desert, threatens many parts of the Sahel. It is caused by overgrazing, cutting trees and long droughts." What is desertification?
questions.label: 13. Read: "Desertification, the process by which fertile land becomes desert, threatens many parts of…

similar.q: List two causes of desertification from the passage.
similar.a: overgrazing and cutting trees (also long droughts).

similar.q: Where is desertification a threat, according to the passage?
similar.a: in many parts of the Sahel.

why: Answer B: fertile land turning into desert
The definition follows the word, between commas: "the process by which fertile land becomes desert".
This is a definition context clue.
So the first option is correct.
questions.tip: Use context clues: definitions, synonyms, contrast words (but, unlike, however) and examples (such as). Answer from the passage, not from your own opinion.

questions.q: Read: "The candidate's speech was verbose; it lasted two hours, yet he said very little that was new." What does "verbose" mean?
questions.label: 14. Read: "The candidate's speech was verbose; it lasted two hours, yet he said very little that was…

similar.q: Which word in the passage signals contrast?

why: Answer C: using more words than necessary
The speech "lasted two hours" but "said very little that was new".
This shows too many words for little content.
So verbose means using more words than necessary.
questions.tip: Use context clues: definitions, synonyms, contrast words (but, unlike, however) and examples (such as). Answer from the passage, not from your own opinion.

questions.q: Read: "Many birds migrate. For example, storks fly from Europe to Africa every autumn and return in spring." What does "migrate" mean?
questions.label: 15. Read: "Many birds migrate. For example, storks fly from Europe to Africa every autumn and return in…

options.D: move from one region to another according to the season

why: Answer D: move from one region to another according to the season
The example explains the word: storks fly from Europe to Africa and return.
This shows seasonal movement.
So migrate means move between regions with the seasons.
questions.tip: Use context clues: definitions, synonyms, contrast words (but, unlike, however) and examples (such as). Answer from the passage, not from your own opinion.

questions.q: Read: "Hagos was usually gregarious, chatting with everyone at parties, but after his father's death he became withdrawn and avoided people." What does "gregarious" mean?
questions.label: 16. Read: "Hagos was usually gregarious, chatting with everyone at parties, but after his father's…

similar.a: quiet and not wanting to be with people.

why: Answer D: sociable and fond of company
"chatting with everyone at parties" describes gregarious.
"but ... withdrawn and avoided people" shows the contrast.
So gregarious means sociable.
questions.tip: Use context clues: definitions, synonyms, contrast words (but, unlike, however) and examples (such as). Answer from the passage, not from your own opinion.

questions.q: Read: "Coffee is grown in the highlands of Eritrea. The plants need a cool climate, some shade and well-drained soil. Most beans are picked by hand between October and January." Which statement is true according to the passage?
questions.label: 17. Read: "Coffee is grown in the highlands of Eritrea. The plants need a cool climate, some shade and…

similar.q: What three conditions do coffee plants need?
similar.a: a cool climate, some shade and well-drained soil.

options.B: Coffee grows best in the hot lowlands.
options.D: Coffee beans are mainly picked by hand.

why: Answer D: Coffee beans are mainly picked by hand.
The passage says "Most beans are picked by hand".
It also says coffee needs a cool climate (highlands) and well-drained soil.
It is picked between October and January, not in summer.
questions.tip: Use context clues: definitions, synonyms, contrast words (but, unlike, however) and examples (such as). Answer from the passage, not from your own opinion.

questions.q: Read: "The old bridge was dilapidated: its railings were broken, the planks were rotten and holes appeared after every rain." What does "dilapidated" mean?
questions.label: 18. Read: "The old bridge was dilapidated: its railings were broken, the planks were rotten and holes…

options.A: in very bad condition because of age or neglect

why: Answer A: in very bad condition because of age or neglect
The colon introduces examples: broken railings, rotten planks, holes.
These details show bad condition.
So dilapidated means in very bad condition.
questions.tip: Use context clues: definitions, synonyms, contrast words (but, unlike, however) and examples (such as). Answer from the passage, not from your own opinion.

questions.q: Read: "Ruth was elated when she received the scholarship letter; she jumped, laughed and called all her friends." How did Ruth feel?
questions.label: 19. Read: "Ruth was elated when she received the scholarship letter; she jumped, laughed and called all…
why: Answer B: extremely happy
Jumping, laughing and calling friends show great joy.
These actions are context clues.
So elated means extremely happy.
questions.tip: Use context clues: definitions, synonyms, contrast words (but, unlike, however) and examples (such as). Answer from the passage, not from your own opinion.
